title: Chinese investment in Africa: a double-edged sword for low-carbon industrialisation
summary: Chinese greenfield manufacturing investment raised industrial carbon emissions in Africa, especially when it went into labour- and resource-intensive manufacturing; the same effect does not appear for OECD investment. The authors argue for reshaping Chinese FDI, not discouraging it.
keyPoints: Chinese FDI raised industrial emissions in 34 African countries (2003–2014).
The effect is strongest in labour- and resource-intensive manufacturing.
No such increase is found for FDI from OECD countries.
